source.title: Heterogeneous cytogenetic subgroups and outcomes in childhood acute megakaryoblastic leukemia: a retrospective international study.

description:
In this study, the authors investigated the role of the ETV6::RUNX1 fusion in the diagnosis of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma. B-ALL is a heterogeneous disease, and identifying cytogenetic abnormalities allows accurate stratification into genetically defined subtypes.

The analysis included 342 children diagnosed with B-ALL, among whom 99 cases (28.9%) were positive for the ETV6::RUNX1 fusion, detected using polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based molecular screening. The translocation t(12;21)(p13;q22) results in the fusion of ETV6 (TEL) on chromosome 12 and RUNX1 (AML1) on chromosome 21, creating a chimeric protein that disrupts normal hematopoietic differentiation and contributes to leukemogenesis. The study findings indicate that patients with the ETV6::RUNX1 fusion have a better event-free survival (EFS) compared to those without the fusion. While only 3% of ETV6::RUNX1-positive patients relapsed, the relapse rate in ETV6::RUNX1-negative cases was significantly higher (11.1%). 

This study underscores the diagnostic significance of the ETV6::RUNX1 fusion, highlighting its role as a key molecular marker in pediatric B-ALL.

source.title: Incidence and clinical relevance of TEL/AML1 fusion genes in children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia enrolled in the German and Italian multicenter therapy trials. Associazione Italiana Ematologia Oncologia Pediatrica and the Berlin-Frankfurt-Münster Study Group.

description: This study investigates the diagnostic importance of the translocation t(16;21)(p11;q22), resulting in the TLS/FUS::ERG fusion gene, in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The authors utilized RT-PCR to detect the TLS/FUS::ERG chimeric transcripts in 19 AML cases with the t(16;21)(p11;q22) identified through karyotype analysis. The median age at diagnosis was 22 years (range 2 to 61 years ). The fusion transcript was consistently detected, even during remission, suggesting its role in identifying persistent leukemic cells and potential chemoresistance. The reliable detection of the TLS/FUS::ERG chimeric transcripts at diagnosis demonstrates their utility as a highly sensitive molecular marker for initial AML diagnosis and ongoing disease monitoring. The study also identified a novel transcript variant (Type D), characterized by an additional 138 nucleotides from TLS/FUS exon 8 and ERG exons 7 and 8, which highlights increased molecular heterogeneity in this genetic alteration. This research emphasizes the diagnostic relevance of the t(16;21) translocation across various French-American-British (FAB) subtypes of AML, providing valuable insight for improved diagnostic accuracy in AML patients.

disease.name: Acute Myeloid Leukaemia With FUS::ERG Fusion

source.title: Consistent detection of TLS/FUS-ERG chimeric transcripts in acute myeloid leukemia with t(16;21)(p11;q22) and identification of a novel transcript.

description: This international retrospective study investigates the diagnostic features of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with the t(16;21) translocation resulting in the FUS::ERG fusion gene in pediatric patients. Data were gathered from 14 cohorts within the Berlin-Frankfurt-Münster (I-BFM) Study Group, encompassing 31 cases exhibiting the FUS::ERG with a median age of 9 years (range 2 to 18 years). AML with t(16;21) did not show a predominance in any specific FAB classification and was frequently associated with complex karyotypes, including trisomy 8 and trisomy 10. Notably, FUS::ERG AML often presented with eosinophilia, micromegakaryocytes, and hemophagocytosis. Standard karyotyping may fail to detect the translocation, necessitating the use of more sensitive diagnostic methods such as FISH, RT-PCR, or RNA sequencing. Although 87% of patients achieved remission, 74% experienced relapse, most within the first year, and minimal residual disease (MRD) negativity did not predict relapse-free survival, indicating the presence of chemoresistant leukemic stem cells. Gene expression profiling revealed a distinct molecular signature, with altered retinoic acid signaling, which may offer potential therapeutic targets. The study highlights the unique diagnostic characteristics of AML with t(16;21), reinforcing the need for specialized molecular testing and offering insight into its distinct biological and clinical features.

disease.name: Acute Myeloid Leukaemia With FUS::ERG Fusion

source.title: Prognostic impact of t(16;21)(p11;q22) and t(16;21)(q24;q22) in pediatric AML: a retrospective study by the I-BFM Study Group.

description: In this study, the authors explored the role of retinoic acid receptor alpha (RARα) gene rearrangements in acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) and their connection to the t(15;17) chromosomal translocation. Using molecular and cytogenetic analyses, they examined eight APL patients and the NB4 cell line, derived from an APL patient. The study identified a RARα fusion transcript, formed by the translocation of RARα from chromosome 17 to the partner gene on chromosome 15. Southern blot analysis detected RARα gene rearrangements in six of the eight APL patients, while these alterations were absent in normal and non-APL leukemic controls. These findings strongly implicate RARα in APL leukemogenesis and suggest that the t(15;17) translocation results in a fusion gene that disrupts normal RARα function, contributing to the disease. The study further highlights the importance of molecular testing for RARα rearrangements as a diagnostic marker for APL.

source.title: The t(15;17) translocation of acute promyelocytic leukaemia fuses the retinoic acid receptor alpha gene to a novel transcribed locus.

description: In this study, the authors investigated the role of retinoic acid receptor alpha (RARα) gene rearrangements in acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), a distinct subtype of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) characterized by the t(15;17) chromosomal translocation. The study analyzed 20 APL cases, of which 18 exhibited the t(15;17) translocation, while 2 had a normal karyotype. Using Southern and Northern blot analyses, the authors identified RARα gene rearrangements and aberrant transcripts exclusively in APL cases, but not in other neoplastic conditions or normal controls. These findings suggest that RARα is directly involved in the APL chromosome 17 breakpoint and plays a crucial role in leukemogenesis. The study highlights the diagnostic significance of RARα gene alterations, as their presence can serve as a molecular marker for identifying leukemic promyelocytes in APL.

source.title: Rearrangements and aberrant expression of the retinoic acid receptor alpha gene in acute promyelocytic leukemias.

description:
In this study, the authors characterized the TEL (currently ETV6)::AML1 (currently RUNX1) gene fusion in B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) with the t(12;21)(p12;q22) using cytogenetic and molecular methods, including FISH, PCR, Southern blot hybridization, and sequencing.

Analysis of nine patient specimens (two AML, seven B-ALL) and two cell lines revealed that the TEL (ETV6) gene breakpoint in t(12;21)(p12;q22) differs from the one in t(5;12)(q33;p13) seen in Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia (CMML). The TEL (ETV6) gene remained active on both derivative chromosomes, with der(21) expressing a 5’ ETV6::3'RUNX1 fusion transcript lacking the ETS DNA-binding domain, while der(12) expressed the ETS domain under an unknown promoter (G4). Additionally, ETV6 was deleted from the normal chromosome 12. The breakpoint in the RUNX1 gene was at its 5’ end, upstream of breakpoints in other myeloid malignancies [t(8;21), t(3;21)].                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

The ETV6::RUNX1 fusion protein retained  helix-loop-helix (HLH) domain from the ETV6-encoded protein which interacts with transcriptional regulators, and nearly entire RUNX1-encoded protein. The chimeric protein was predicted to cause dysregulated transcription of lymphoid lineage-specific genes.

These findings provide insight into the molecular mechanisms of  ETV6::RUNX1-driven leukemogenesis in B-ALL.

source.title: The t(12;21) of acute lymphoblastic leukemia results in a tel-AML1 gene fusion.

description:
In this study, the authors investigated the t(12;21)(p13;q22) in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). The t(12;21) is typically not visible by karyotype analysis and is rarely detected by conventional cytogenetics (<0.05% of cases). However, using molecular techniques, the authors identified the resulting TEL::AML1 (known currently as ETV6::RUNX1) fusion transcript in 22% of pediatric ALL patients, making it the most frequent genetic alteration in this disease.

The TEL::AML1 (ETV6::RUNX1) fusion results from the rearrangement of TEL (ETV6), a helix-loop-helix ETS-like transcription factor, and AML1 (RUNX1), the DNA-binding subunit of the core-binding factor (CBF) transcription complex.  

Patients harboring the TEL::AML1 (ETV6::RUNX1) fusion exhibited distinct clinical features, including an age range of 1 to 10 years, B-lineage immunophenotype, non-hyperdiploid DNA content, and an excellent prognosis. These findings underscore the role of ETV6::RUNX1 fusion in defining a common and clinically relevant subtype of pediatric B-ALL.

source.title: TEL/AML1 fusion resulting from a cryptic t(12;21) is the most common genetic lesion in pediatric ALL and defines a subgroup of patients with an excellent prognosis.

description: In this 2016 study the authors included 153 pediatric non-Down syndrome patients diagnosed with acute megakaryoblastic leukemia (AMKL) which is a rare subtype of acute myeloid leukemia. All patients were screened for NUP98::KDM5A, CBFA2T3::GLIS2, RBM15::MKL1 and KMT2A rearrangements with polymerase chain reaction (PCR). The PCR primers for NUP98::KDM5A were designed to detect a NUP98 exon 12 fusion to exon 27 of KDM5A. The NUP98::KDM5A gene fusion was detected in 14 patients (9%) with a median age of 1.9 years (range 0.8-8.5); it was mutually exclusive with other tested fusions and its' presence was associated with an unfavorable outcome. The NUP98::KDM5A fusion is the primary abnormality in a subtype of pediatric AML commonly presenting with magakaryoblastic differentiation and associated with a poor clinical outcome.

disease.name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With NUP98 Rearrangement

source.title: Recurrent abnormalities can be used for risk group stratification in pediatric AMKL: a retrospective intergroup study.

description: In this 2011 study the authors included pediatric and adult cohorts of patients diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Initially, using RT-PCR, they detected the cytogenetically cryptic NUP98::NSD1 in-frame gene fusion of NUP98 exon 12 to exon 6 of NSD1 in 2/45 pediatric cytogenetically normal AML (CN-AML) patients and in 1/47 adult CN-AML cases. A further 1101 AML cases were then screened using RT-PCR and the identical NUP98::NSD1 in-frame fusion was detected in 23 (2.1%) cases. The NUP98::NSD1 fusion was detected more frequently in pediatric patients with a median age of onset at 17 years (range 2 to 63), and was particularly frequent in children when considering only the CN-AML cases. Three additional cases with cytogenetically visible 11p15-aberrations were also confirmed to have NUP98 gene fusions, however with alternate partners including JARID1A, TOP1 and DDX10. NUP98::NSD1 was frequently associated with FLT3 ITD (91% of cases) and WT1 mutations (45% of cases). The authors conclude that the cryptic NUP98::NSD1 fusion defines a previously unrecognized group of young AML patients associated with an unfavorable outcome and routine screening for NUP98::NSD1 at diagnosis is essential.

disease.name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With NUP98 Rearrangement

source.title: NUP98/NSD1 characterizes a novel poor prognostic group in acute myeloid leukemia with a distinct HOX gene expression pattern.

description: In this 2014 study the authors investigated the presence of NUP98::NSD1 fusion in pediatric and adult acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients. Utilizing reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) the NUP98::NSD1 fusion was identified in 39/920 (4%) patients. Since 36 of the 39 NUP98::NSD1 patients were either FLT3 ITD positive or cytogenetically normal (CN-AML) a further 620 patients who harbored FLT3 ITD and/or CN-AML were included for screening, with the NUP98::NSD1 identified  in 63 (10%) patients. All patients harbored the identical in-frame fusion of NUP98 exon 12 and NSD1 exon 6. Age of patients with NUP98::NSD1 varied from <1 to 50 years of age (median, 10 years), indicating that NUP98::NSD1 is more frequent in younger age. NUP98::NSD1 cases frequently (82%) harbored a FLT3 ITD, and 26% harbored simultaneously FLT3 ITD and WT1 mutations. The authors conclude that the NUP98::NSD1 fusion, frequently co-occurring with FLT3 ITD, defines a subgroup of AML patients at very high risk for induction failure; the study supports upfront screening of CN-AML for the cytogenetically cryptic NUP98::NSD1 fusion.

disease.name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With NUP98 Rearrangement

source.title: NUP98/NSD1 and FLT3/ITD coexpression is more prevalent in younger AML patients and leads to induction failure: a COG and SWOG report.

description: In this 2023 study the authors included 2,235 children and young adults diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). NUP98 fusions were detected in these patients either by karyotype of RNA sequencing. Overall 160 patients (7.2%) were identified to have a NUP98 rearrangement. The most common NUP98 translocations were NUP98::NSD1 (108/160) and NUP98::KDM5A (32/160), however 20 patients were detected with 13 different NUP98 translocation partners, including HOXA9 (n=4), HOXD13 (n=3), PHF15 (n=2), PHF23 (n=2) and single cases of BPTF, BRWD3, DDX10, HMGB3, HOXA13, KAT7, PRRX1, SET, and TOP1. NUP98 fusions were enriched in children aged 3-10 years old. NUP98 fusion breakpoints by RNA sequencing revealed a high diversity of NUP98 exon junctions, although 85% of NUP98 fusions had a breakpoint junction in exon 12 or 13, the remaining cases had breakpoints occurring in various positions from exon 11 to exon 29. The NUP98::KDM5A immunophenotype corresponded to megakaryocytic maturation. For NUP98:NSD1 cases, enrichment of FLT3 ITD (74%) and WT1 mutations (42%) was detected. The authors conclude that NUP98 fusions constitute a highly refractory class of AML, regardless of fusion partner.

disease.name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With NUP98 Rearrangement

source.title: Comprehensive molecular and clinical characterization of NUP98 fusions in pediatric acute myeloid leukemia.

description: This MD Anderson Cancer Center study describes six adult patients (3 males and 3 females, median age 39 yo) with t(14;19)(q32;p13) resulting in IGH::EPOR. 3 patients did not receive any prior chemotherapy, whereas 3 presented with refractory/relapsed disease post-induction. Major symptoms at presentation: fatique, lower extremity swelling, bone pain; 3 patients had splenomegaly. No CNS involvement or extramedullary disease. The median Hb 8.8 g/dl, median PLT count 31 k/ul. All patients had circulating blasts, increased serum lactate dehydrogenase levels and serum beta-2-microglobulin level. Blast morphology: variably condensed chromatin, prominent nucleoli, agranular cytoplasm. Marrow was hypercellular for all patients, with median blast count at 90%. Flow consistent with precursor B-cell immunophenotype: CD10+, CD19+, CD20+, CD22+, CD34+, CD38+, HLA-DR+, TdT+, CD1a-, CD2-, CD3 (surface and cytoplasmic), CD4-, CD5-, CD7-, CD8-, CD14-, CD15-, CD25-, CD41-, CD56-, CD117-, MPO-. Chromosome analysis revealed t(14;19)(q32;p13) in all 6 patients, 2 patients had complex karyotype. FISH with IGH and EPOR probes showed 1F on der(14). All patients received combination chemo, but all relapsed, 5/6 died after 12 months. The manuscript describes clinical, morphologic, immunophenotypic and genetic characteristics of B-ALL  caused by EPOR rearrangments with the IGH locus, which are rare primary drivers in B-ALL with BCR::ABL1 like features.

source.title: B acute lymphoblastic leukemia with t(14;19)(q32;p13.1) involving IGH/EPOR: a clinically aggressive subset of disease.

description: This 2017 study is result of collaboration of multiple institutions and was led by St. Jude Children's Research Hospital team. The total cohort of 3115 B-ALL patients (all ages) was studied, with 212 with expression profile of BCR::ABL1-like B-ALL (based on gemone and/or transcriptome sequencing). 19 out of 212 cases (8.9%) revealed 4 types of EPOR rearrangements: insertion of EPOR distal to the IGH enhancer (73.7%), insertion of EPOR into IGK at 2p11.2 (10.5%), cytogenetically visible t(14;19)(q32;p13) (10.5%), and insertion of EPOR upstream of LAIR1 (leukocyte-associated immunoglobulin-like receptor 1) at 19q13 (5.3%). The authors demonstrated that all these EPOR rearrangements resulted in truncation of the cytoplasmic tail of EPOR with preservation of Y368 tyrosine residue essential for receptor activation and loss of distal regulatory tyrosine residues (Y426, Y454, Y456, Y504) and resulted in JAK/STAT signaling activation (potential for treatment). All EPORr cases showed no expression distal to the rearrangement by ex8 specific assay (potential for screening). Interestingly, the authors used 3 EPORr cases to isolate leukemic, stem cell, progenitor, mature cell populations to test for EPORr, which was identified not only in blasts, but also in CD33+ myeloid cells (all 3 cases), myeloid progenitors (1 case), and even in normal B-cell obtained at the time of remission in 1 case. The study described genomic structure of EPOR rearrangements in B-ALL and confirmed their association with B-ALL with BCR::ABL1-like features.

source.title: Truncating Erythropoietin Receptor Rearrangements in Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.

description: In this 2018 study the authors include 1,023 young people diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The age at presentation for the participants ranged from 0 to 29 years (median of 10 years). The presence of KMT2A rearrangements was determined from manual review of available cytogenetic results, combined with genome sequencing and RNA-sequencing findings from the study. A cytogenetic KMT2A abnormality was detected in 38% of infants (less than 3 year of age), 13% of children (aged 3 to 14 years), and 11% of adolescent and young adults (aged 15 to 29 years). Multiple KMT2A fusion partners were detected, with MLLT3 occurring most frequently. The study illustrates that KMT2A rearrangements define a subtype of AML common in children and young adults.

disease.name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MLL Rearrangement
diseaseAliases: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With KMT2A/MLL Rearrangement

source.title: The molecular landscape of pediatric acute myeloid leukemia reveals recurrent structural alterations and age-specific mutational interactions.

description: In this 2024 study the authors included patient data from 1256 children (aged less than 19 years) across 15 different countries diagnosed with KMT2A rearranged acute myeloid leukemia (AML). KMT2A rearrangements were detected by cytogenetics, with some confirmed by fluorescence in situ hybridization, or reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, within the local centers. Multiple KMT2A fusion partners were detected, with KMT2A::MLLT3 (n = 544, 43.3%), KMT2A::MLLT10 (n = 218, 17.4%), KMT2A::AFDN (n = 92, 7.3%), and KMT2A::ELL (n = 75, 6.0%) most frequent, together accounting for around 75% of cases. The authors found that different fusion partners, morphology and/or additional cytogenetic abnormalities may impact outcomes.

disease.name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MLL Rearrangement
diseaseAliases: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With KMT2A/MLL Rearrangement

source.title: Optimized cytogenetic risk-group stratification of KMT2A-rearranged pediatric acute myeloid leukemia.

description: In this 2023 publication the authors include 3401 KMT2A rearranged leukemia samples obtained from different diagnostic centers worldwide, and subject them to DNA sequence analyses. Of these patients, 1116 were diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML), including 197 patients aged less than 12 months, 465 patients aged 1 to 18 years and 441 patients older than 18 years (for 13 patients age was unknown). AML patients displayed a diverse number of partner genes with MLLT3 (n = 339; 30.4%) and MLLT10 (n = 209; 18.7%) the most common. KMT2A rearrangements typically involve in-frame fusions with KMT2A as the 5' partner and KMT2A breakpoints in AML patients almost always occur somewhere between intron 7 and exon 13 (NM_001412597.1). KMT2A-partial tandem in-frame duplications that involve the N-terminus can also occur, mostly frequently in AML in adult patients.

diseaseAliases: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With KMT2A/MLL Rearrangement

source.title: The KMT2A recombinome of acute leukemias in 2023.

description: The authors studied 27 archival formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) cases obtained from Texas Children's Hospital and University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center. The cases included 16 females and 11 males with an age range of 1-73 years and diagnosed with DFSP and diffuse expression of CD34 by immunohistochemistry. Using a highly sensitive multiplex RT-PCR-direct sequencing assay developed for FFPE tissue, the authors detected COL1A1-PDGFB fusion transcripts with 18 different COL1A1 forward primers spanning the α-helical domain (exons 5-49) and a single PDGFB reverse primer. Break-apart FISH was performed using BAC DNA clones mapping centromeric and telomeric of the PGDFB locus. Sequencing analysis confirmed in-frame fusion of exon 2 of PDGFB to different breakpoints in COL1A1 (exons 7, 10, 29, 40, 46, and 49 and introns between exons 13:14, 26:27, 30:31, 33:34, 43:44, 45:46, 46:47). Of these, COL1A1 breakpoints in exon 49 and in introns between exons 13:14 and 30:31, are novel. Using both RT-PCR and FISH techniques, the authors report a higher prevalence of COL1A1-PDGFB rearrangements (96%) in DFSP cases than reported in earlier studies, and attribute this to the high sensitivity of their multiplex RT-PCR direct sequencing assay. Testing FFPE specimen with both FISH and RT-PCR would prove helpful for the differential diagnosis of atypical, fibrosarcomatous and metastatic DFSP.

source.title: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans COL1A1-PDGFB fusion is identified in virtually all dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans cases when investigated by newly developed multiplex reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and fluorescence in situ hybridization assays.

description: In this study, paraffin-embedded tissue microarray (TMA) evaluation of translocation t(17;22)(q22;q13) was performed on 40 tissue samples from 24 female and 16 male DFSP patients (37 primary tumors, 3 local recurrences) obtained from 3 hospitals in Barcelona, Spain. The median age of these DFSP patients was 43 y and the age range was 15-87 y. A second tissue microarray included 20 samples from dermatofibroma (DF) patients. Samples from 6 postsurgical scars were used as negative controls. FISH was performed using dual-color dual-fusion BAC clones to detect the cytogenetic COL1A1-PDGFB translocation. From the evaluable 29 DFSP cases, 86% (n=25) showed the COL1A1-PDGFB FISH signal pattern, which was absent in all DF control cases and in the 6 scars. Of these 25 COL1A1-PDGFB positive DFSP cases, 19 showed multiple (more than 3) copies of the translocation. Tumor size correlated positively with a higher proportion of DFSP tumor cells showing the fusion signal, and DFSPs with fibrosarcomatous areas (DFSP-FS) also showed cells with 6 or more COL1A1-PDGFB gene fusions signals.

source.title: Identification of t(17;22)(q22;q13) (COL1A1/PDGFB) in dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans by fluorescence in situ hybridization in paraffin-embedded tissue microarrays.

description: A cross-sectional cohort study was performed in 161 men with metastatic prostate cancer undergoing a change in treatment to determine if pre-therapy AR-V7 nuclear protein expression in circulating tumor cells (CTCs) is a treatment-specific marker for outcomes between androgen receptor signaling (ARS) inhibitors and taxanes. A multivariable model adjusting for baseline factor associated with survival showed superior overall survival with taxanes relative to ARS inhibitors when AR-V7-positive CTCs were detected pre-therapy (hazard ratio , 0.24; 95% CI 0.10-0.57; P=0.035).

source.title: Association of AR-V7 on Circulating Tumor Cells as a Treatment-Specific Biomarker With Outcomes and Survival in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer.

description: A blinded, multi-institutional cohort study was performed in 142 men with metastatic, castration-resistant prostate cancer to determine if pre-therapy nuclear-localized expression of AR-V7 protein in circulating tumor cells (CTCs) is a treatment-selective marker for outcome following treatment with either androgen receptor signaling (ARS) inhibitors or taxanes. Patients with AR-V7-positive CTCs had superior overall survival with taxanes vs ARS inhibitors (hazard ratio 0.62; 95% CI 0.28-1.39; P=.25). Patients with AR-V7-negative CTCs had superior overall survival with ARS inhibitors vs taxanes (hazard ratio 1.67; 95 CI 1.00-2.81); P=.05).

source.title: Assessment of the Validity of Nuclear-Localized Androgen Receptor Splice Variant 7 in Circulating Tumor Cells as a Predictive Biomarker for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer.

description: In this 2017 study, the authors analyzed 91 pediatric B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (BCP-ALL) patients and an additional 122 classified as "B-others" lacking conventional genetic abnormalities. ZNF384 rearrangements were identified through whole transcriptome sequencing and PCR-based fusion detection. ZNF384-related fusions were detected in 4.1% of all BCP-ALL cases (9.2% of B-others), with TCF3::ZNF384 being most frequent (2.4% overall). The leukemic cells exhibited a characteristic immunophenotype of weak/absent CD10 and aberrant CD13/CD33 expression, distinct from ZNF384-fusion negative cases. Gene expression profiling revealed enrichment of hematopoietic stem cell features in TCF3::ZNF384 cases, differing from TCF3-PBX1-positive ALL. Clinically, TCF3-ZNF384 patients presented with higher leukocyte counts and poorer steroid response compared to EP300-ZNF384 cases, suggesting fusion partner-dependent heterogeneity. The study demonstrates that ZNF384 rearrangements define a molecularly distinct BCP-ALL subgroup with diagnostic immunophenotypic features, while clinical outcomes vary by fusion partner.

disease.name: B-lymphoblastic Leukaemia/lymphoma With Other Defined Genetic Alterations

source.title: ZNF384-related fusion genes define a subgroup of childhood B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia with a characteristic immunotype.

description: In this study, the authors used long-distance inverse PCR and sequencing to comprehensively analyze KMT2A (MLL) gene rearrangements in 2,345 acute leukemia patients, including those with B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL). The findings reinforce the diagnostic significance of KMT2A rearrangements in B-ALL, particularly in infants and young children. The study identified 135 distinct KMT2A rearrangements involving 94 translocation partner genes (TPGs); of those, only 9 fusions accounted for over 90% of the cases, including KMT2A::AFF1, KMT2A::MLLT1, and KMT2A::MLLT3. Among B-ALL patients, the KMT2A::AFF1 (AF4) fusion was the most frequent, especially in infants, followed by KMT2A::MLLT1 (ENL) and KMT2A::MLLT3 (AF9). Importantly, the study highlighted an age-dependent breakpoint shift within the KMT2A locus, with intron 11 breakpoints associated more frequently with B-ALL in younger patients, and intron 9 breakpoints found more often in AML and older patients. This study supports the classification of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with KMT2A rearrangement as a distinct diagnostic entity independent of the fusion partner; this is recognized in the WHO 5th edition (2022) and the International Consensus Classification.

source.title: The MLL recombinome of acute leukemias in 2017.

description:
In this publication, the authors conducted a comprehensive genomic analysis of 2,754 pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) cases using integrated whole genome, exome, and transcriptome sequencing. Of the 2,288 B-ALL cases analyzed, KMT2A rearrangements were identified in approximately 4.5%, confirming their role as a recurrent driver in pediatric B-ALL. These KMT2A-rearranged cases were characterized by a low somatic mutational burden, distinct gene expression profiles, and unique biological features compared to other B-ALL subtypes.
The study revealed multiple KMT2A fusion partners, with recurrent fusions involving genes such as MLLT1, MLLT3, AFF1, and others, reinforcing that the diagnostic significance lies in the presence of the KMT2A rearrangement itself, irrespective of the fusion partner. Further sub-classification based on transcriptome clustering identified two transcriptionally distinct KMT2A subgroups—one enriched for NFATC4 expression and the other for CEBPA/FLT3 expression—suggesting underlying differences in developmental origin and potential clinical implications.
These findings support the recognition of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with KMT2A rearrangement as a distinct diagnostic entity, consistent with the updated 2022 International Consensus Classification (ICC) and the 2024 World Health Organization (WHO) classification.

source.title: The genomic landscape of pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

description:
In this publication, the diagnostic significance of KMT2A rearrangements in B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL) is explored. The study reveals that KMT2A fusions are not restricted to lymphoid lineages but may also involve myeloid compartments and hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPCs), supporting a multilineage origin in a substantial proportion of cases. Notably, 36% of patients with KMT2A-rearranged B-ALL exhibited evidence of multilineage involvement at diagnosis.

This finding has important diagnostic implications, as conventional MRD assessment strategies—relying on flow cytometry or immunoglobulin gene rearrangement—may fail to detect residual disease in cases where leukemic clones persist in non-lymphoid compartments. RNA sequencing data further demonstrate a gene expression profile enriched for HSPC and myeloid programs in these patients, reinforcing the hybrid lineage biology of KMT2A-rearranged B-ALL. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating molecular techniques such as fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) or RNA-based assays to detect KMT2A fusions as key diagnostic markers in this B-ALL subtype.

source.title: Multilineage involvement in KMT2A-rearranged B acute lymphoblastic leukaemia: cell-of-origin, biology, and clinical implications.

description: In this 2005 study, immunohistochemical staining was used to assess the subcellular localization of NPM in 1,835 paraffin-embedded tumor specimens, including 591 from primary AML patients (ages 15–60), 135 from secondary AML patients, and 980 from hematopoietic and non-hematopoietic neoplasms other than AML. Of the 591 specimens tested, 208 (35.2%) were found to have aberrant cytoplasmic NPM localization (NPMc+), while the remainder displayed normal nuclear localization (NPMc–). Subsequent RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing found 51/52 NPMc+ specimens harbored a NPM1 exon 11 (NM_002520) mutation that results in a distinct C-terminal sequence and is predicted to alter the NPM protein at its C-terminus (referred to in this study as NPM exon 12 mutations). Transfection of NIH-3T3 cells with the NPM1 mutant alleles showed aberrant cytoplasmic localization compared to wild type, demonstrating a causal relationship between NPM1 mutation status and aberrant subcellular localization. NPMc+ was found to be associated with a normal karyotype in approximately 60% of AML patients (142/230, 61.7%). FLT3 internal tandem duplications were found to be twice as frequent in NPMc+ vs. NPMc- specimens, suggesting these mutations may be mechanistically linked. The majority of NPMc+ AML specimens were CD34- (49/52) and had a wide morphologic spectrum, demonstrating multilineage involvement. Finally, the authors investigated the response to induction therapy in 126 patients with AML and a normal karyotype (79 NPMc+, 47 NPMc-) treated according to the GIMEMA LAM99P protocol. AML patients with a normal karyotype and NPMc+ were found to have a relatively good response to induction chemotherapy. The study illustrates that AML cases characterized by NPM1 mutations represent a unique disease subtype with shared morphologic features, immunophenotype  and molecular and clinical characteristics.

disease.name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With Mutated NPM1

source.title: Cytoplasmic nucleophosmin in acute myelogenous leukemia with a normal karyotype.

description: In this 2017 study the author included 44 cellular myofibroblastic tumors previously diagnosed as cellular myofibroma, cellular myopericytoma, or cellular myofibroblastic neoplasms (NOS), and a control group of 34 various myofibroblastic lesions, including typical myofibromas (adult and infantile variants), myopericytomas, malignant myopericytomas, low grade myofibroblastic sarcomas, and myofibroblastomas. RT-PCR and FISH was utilised to investigate SRF gene abnormalities. SRF gene rearrangements were detected in 10 cases of cellular myofibroblastic tumors and not detected in any of the control group, including classic examples of both myofibroma and myopericytoma. SRF::RELA fusions were present in 7 tumours, while another case had a SRF::C3orf62 fusion and in two cases the partner was not identified. RT-PCR confirmed fusion of SRF exon 4 with RELA exon 11 in one case. The cohort was composed of 7 females and 3 males, with a wide age range at diagnosis, of 3 months to 63 years (mean 17; median 14), the majority under the age of 18 years. The anatomic distribution was quite broad. The authors concluded that they have identified a subset of cellular myofibroblastic tumors occurring mostly in children and young adults, with morphologic features in keeping with cellular variants of myofibroma and myopericytoma, and harboring recurrent gene rearrangements in the SRF gene which in the majority of these cases resulted in SRF::RELA gene fusions.

source.title: Recurrent SRF-RELA Fusions Define a Novel Subset of Cellular Myofibroma/Myopericytoma: A Potential Diagnostic Pitfall With Sarcomas With Myogenic Differentiation.

description: In this 2020 study, the authors include 13 perivascular myoid tumors belonging to the previously described SRF rearranged subtype of tumors (PMID:28248815), which share morphologic features with myopericytomas and myofibromas and express smooth muscle markers similarly to most perivascular myoid tumors. The cohort was composed of 6 males and 7 females, and all patients except 1 were pediatric, with a mean age of 11.8 years (ranging from 1  week to 73  years). RNA-sequencing was successfully performed on 12 samples and detected the SRF::RELA fusion in 6 tumors, SRF::NCOA2 in 3 tumors, while SRF::CITED1, SRF::NFKBIE, and CITED2::SRF were detected once. The breakpoints were located in exons (ENST00000265354) 2 to 5 of the SRF gene. The tumors occurred in different anatomic sites, although often tumors (n=8) were situated in the head. Follow-up data showed that tumors seem to be nonaggressive. The authors concluded that they have expanded the molecular spectrum of the perivascular tumors with SRF rearrangement by identifying 4 additional fusion genes and suggest naming the distinct clinicopathologic entity SRF-fused perivascular tumor.

source.title: SRF Fusions Other Than With RELA Expand the Molecular Definition of SRF-fused Perivascular Tumors.

description:
In this Swedish population-based study, the authors retrospectively re-evaluated 71 poorly differentiated supratentorial CNS tumors in children, previously diagnosed as CNS-PNETs, to assess their molecular features, including BCOR genetic alterations. The cohort included 39 males and 32 females, with a median age at diagnosis of 6.2 years. Using WHO 2021 histopathological guidelines and the Molecular Neuropathology (MNP) brain tumor classifier, 10% (n=7) of tumors were subclassified as CNS neuroblastoma with FOXR2 activation (CNS NB-FOXR2). All seven CNS NB-FOXR2 tumors showed complete concordance between histology-based diagnoses and DNA methylation-based classification, with a calibrated score (CS) ≥ 0.9.
The median age at diagnosis of CNS NB-FOXR2 patients was 5.3 years (range 2.5–15.7), with 43% males (n=3) and 57% females (n=4). Copy number analysis predicted gain of chromosome 1q in all seven tumors, and whole or partial loss of chromosome 16q in 86% (6/7) of cases. While the overall CNS-PNET cohort demonstrated poor outcomes (5-year PFS 38% ±11%, 5-year OS 45% ±12%), CNS NB-FOXR2 patients had excellent prognosis, with both 5-year PFS and OS at 100%.
These findings highlight that CNS NB-FOXR2 represents a rare, molecularly distinct entity within pediatric CNS-PNETs, and that DNA methylation profiling provides a reliable diagnostic tool to accurately identify this tumor type, which is associated with favorable long-term outcomes.

disease.name: CNS Neuroblastoma With FOXR2 Activation
diseaseAliases: Central Nervous System Neuroblastoma With FOXR2 Activation

source.title: Supratentorial CNS-PNETs in children; a Swedish population-based study with molecular re-evaluation and long-term follow-up.

description:
In this 2016 study, the authors analyzed 398 newly diagnosed Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML) patients, identifying 12 (3%) cases that lacked the Philadelphia (Ph) chromosome by conventional cytogenetic analysis but were positive for the BCR::ABL1 fusion by RT-PCR. Six Ph– cases were further characterized to investigate the cytogenetic mechanisms responsible for this rearrangement. FISH analysis revealed cryptic insertions between chromosomes 9 and 22 in five patients and a classic two-step translocation in one patient, demonstrating four distinct fusion signal patterns and highlighting significant genetic heterogeneity among Ph– CML cases.
The study found that the BCR::ABL1 fusion most frequently localized to chromosome 9q34 rather than the typical 22q11.2 region, contrasting with prior reports. These findings established that even in the absence of the visible Philadelphia chromosome, the presence of the BCR::ABL1 fusion gene serves as a definitive diagnostic hallmark of CML. The authors concluded that detection of BCR::ABL1 by FISH or molecular analysis is essential for confirming the diagnosis of CML in patients with a normal karyotype, supporting its role as the primary molecular event defining the disease.

source.title: Cryptic BCR-ABL fusion gene as variant rearrangement in chronic myeloid leukemia: molecular cytogenetic characterization and influence on TKIs therapy.

description:
This retrospective study examined the association between TMB and clinical response to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) across multiple cancer types. 

1,662 advanced cancer patients treated with at least one dose of ICI, including avelumab, durvalumab, ipilimumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab or tremelimumab as monotherapy or in combination (146 received anti-CTLA-4, 1,256 received anti-PD-1 or PD-L1, and 260 received the combination), were included in the study. Tumour-derived and matched normal germline DNA were sequenced using the MSK-IMPACT targeted 468-cancer gene panel. TMB was calculated as the number of somatic nonsynonymous per megabase sequences. 

Using top 20% within each cancer type as the cutoff, a significant association of improved overall survival with higher TMB was observed in patients with bladder (n=214, p=0.040), colorectal (n=110, p= 0.031), head and neck (n=138, p=7.42 × 10e-3), and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (n=350, p= 2.30× 10e-4), and across the whole cohort (n=1,662, p= 1.59 × 10e-6). A similar trend was also observed in breast cancer (n=45), esophagogastric cancer (n=126), melanoma (n=321), renal cell carcinoma (n=151), and cancer of unknown primary (n=90), despite not reaching statistical significance. This association was also observed using different cut points ranging between top10-50% to define high TMB. Similarly, improved clinical benefit/ progression free survival were also associated higher TMB among patients with NSCLC, melanoma, esophagogastric, head and neck, and renal cell carcinoma. Notably, distinct from these cancer types, no association between higher TMB and improved patient survival was observed in glioma (n=117). 

A cohort of 5,371 advanced cancer patients who did not receive ICI were also included in this study. A lack of prognostic benefit of TMB status was observed both across the cancer types and within each histology, demonstrating the observed survival difference among patients with TMB high tumours was attributed to ICI treatment. 

The authors also noted that stratifying by TMB decile within histology was chosen in this study to demonstrate the relationship between TMB and patient prognosis, although this method may not be ideal for clinical use.

Overall, this study demonstrated the clinical value of higher TMB in predicting superior overall survival in patients across multiple cancer types. However, the authors also noted that stratifying by TMB decile within histology was chosen in this study to demonstrate the relationship between TMB and patient prognosis, although this method may not be ideal for clinical use.

source.title: Tumor mutational load predicts survival after immunotherapy across multiple cancer types.

description: High Tumor Mutation Burden (TMB >19 mutations/Mb) represents a robust and platform-validated genomic biomarker predictive of clinical benefit from PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint blockade in non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This threshold was derived through regression tree modeling across multiple sequencing platforms (MSK-IMPACT, DFCI-OncoPanel, and whole-exome sequencing) and validated in three large, independent cohorts totaling 1,552 patients. Patients with high TMB demonstrated significantly improved objective response rate (49.1% vs 21.5%, p<0.001), progression-free survival (11.4 vs 2.8 months, p<0.001), and overall survival (36.1 vs 12.4 months, p<0.001) compared with those with low TMB, independent of PD-L1 expression levels. Molecular and immune profiling revealed that high-TMB NSCLCs exhibit enhanced CD8⁺ and PD-1⁺ T-cell infiltration, increased PD-L1 expression, and activation of antigen presentation pathways. The authors suggested that TMB >19 mut/Mb is a clinically actionable biomarker for identifying NSCLC patients most likely to respond to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors.

source.title: Association of High Tumor Mutation Burden in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancers With Increased Immune Infiltration and Improved Clinical Outcomes of PD-L1 Blockade Across PD-L1 Expression Levels.

description: This retrospective study evaluated the clinical utility of blood tumour mutational burden (bTMB) as a predictive biomarker for atezolizumab efficacy in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who had progressed from first-line therapy using samples collected prospectively from 2 randomized trials. The cfDNA assay used in this study utilised the same 1.1 Mb tissue FoundationOne hybridization capture panel (394 genes). The bTMB score was calculated by identifying all base substitutions present at an allele frequency of ≥0.5%, with predicted germline variants filtered out. Pre-treatment plasma bTMB demonstrated a positive correlation with the patient-paired tissue TMB (tTMB) (Spearman rank correlation = 0.64, n=259). Based on this correlation, an optimal cut-off point of ≥ 16 mutations per megabase (with a minimum somatic allele frequency ≥ 1%) was selected for subsequent clinical evaluation. Applying the cut off of bTMB ≥ 16 mutations per megabase to the POPLAR study (NCT01903993) (n=211) demonstrated improved progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) benefit with atezolizumab versus docetaxel. At this cut-off, the PFS hazard ratio (HR) was 0.57. The median PFS was 4.2 months in the atezolizumab arm and 2.9 months in the docetaxel arm; the median OS values were 13.0 and 7.4 months, respectively. The biomarker-treatment interaction for PFS at bTMB ≥ 16 trended towards significance (interaction P = 0.055). The predictive value was independently validated in the larger OAK study (NCT02008227) (n=583). Patients bTMB ≥16 muts/Mb showed significant PFS benefit from atezolizumab (HR: 0.65, P=0.013), with the biomarker-treatment interaction for PFS being statistically significant (P=0.036). Although the OS benefit in this subgroup was substantial (median 13.5 versus 6.8 months, HR: 0.64), the treatment interaction for overall survival was not significant. The findings support bTMB ≥16 mutations per megabase as a non-invasive biomarker for predicting enhanced PFS benefit from atezolizumab in advanced NSCLC patients who have progressed on first-line therapy.

source.title: Blood-based tumor mutational burden as a predictor of clinical benefit in non-small-cell lung cancer patients treated with atezolizumab.

description:
In this 2009 study, the authors included 336 chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) patients at diagnosis, of which 25 patients (7.44%) exhibited variant Philadelphia (Ph) chromosome translocations. A control group of patients with the standard t(9;22) translocation was used for comparison. Conventional cytogenetics and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) were utilized to characterize the variant translocations and investigate deletions on the derivative chromosome 9 [der(9)].
Variant Ph translocations, involving chromosomes 9, 22, and one or more additional chromosomes, were identified in all 25 cases. The BCR::ABL1 fusion gene was detected in all patients, confirming the diagnosis of CML despite the complex karyotypes. Deletions adjacent to the ABL1 gene on der(9) were observed in 15 of the 25 cases (60%), a significantly greater proportion than that found in typical Ph translocations (12–15%). The genesis of these variants was attributed to both one-step (36%) and two-step (56%) mechanisms, with the latter being more prevalent. The cohort was composed of patients where any chromosome could be involved, with breakpoints preferentially located in the CG-richest regions of the genome.
The authors concluded that the BCR::ABL1 fusion is the fundamental diagnostic event in CML, even in cases with complex variant translocations. They identified that these variant translocations are associated with a markedly higher incidence of deletions on der(9). Proper assessment of the prognostic significance of these variants requires categorization based on their mechanism of genesis and 9q34 deletion status.

source.title: Molecular cytogenetic characterization of variant Philadelphia translocations in chronic myeloid leukemia: genesis and deletion of derivative chromosome 9.

description: This study analyzed over 300 patient with advanced solid tumors and melanoma across 22 tumor types from four KEYNOTE clinical trials to define genomic and immune predictors of response to pembrolizumab (anti–PD-1 immunotherapy). Using whole-exome sequencing and NanoString gene profiling, they evaluated tumor mutational burden (TMB) and the T cell–inflamed gene expression profile (GEP) in formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded pretreatment samples. TMB cut-off values for the pan-tumor and single-indication clinical cohorts were the Youden Index values derived in AUROC analysis (102.5 for pan-cancer, 86 for HNSCC, and 191.5 for melanoma group). TMB and GEP profiles were also analyzed within The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database of 6384 tumors and the WES cut-off >100 mutations per exome was chosen for high TMB to match the Youden TBM pan-cancer cut-offs. TMB and GEP were independently predictive of clinical response and progression-free survival in KEYNOTE cohorts, and together they stratified patients into four biologically distinct subgroups: those with high TMB/high GEP had the highest objective response rates (37–57%), and the longest progression-free survival, whereas those with low TMB/high GEP or high TMB/low GEP showed moderate response rate (12-35% and 11-42%, respectively), and patients with low TMB/low GEP tumors rarely responded (0–9%). The two markers were only weakly correlated (Spearman correlation coefficient at r ~ 0.2), indicating that TMB and GEP are independent predictive markers, with TMB capturing neoantigen load, while GEP reflecting T-cell activation within the tumor microenvironment. Integrative analyses of TCGA data confirmed these findings and revealed resistance-associated alterations such as mutation in STK11, KEAP1, and APC in high TMB and low GEP lung and colorectal cancers, but not in the pan-cancer analysis. In addition, TMB highly correlated with neoantigen load in pan-cancer cohort (r=0.87), HNSCC (r=0.83), and melanoma cohort (r=0.9). Overall, the study established TMB and GEP as complementary, tumor-agnostic predictors of benefit from PD-1 blockade and provided a framework for precision immunotherapy and biomarker-guided combination strategies.

source.title: Pan-tumor genomic biomarkers for PD-1 checkpoint blockade-based immunotherapy.

description: In a randomized, double blind, placebo controlled adjuvant trial in colorectal carcinoma with PI3K pathway mutations (ALASCCA, NCT02647099; group B n = 312), aspirin 160 mg daily (group B n = 156) for 3 years reduced 3 year recurrence vs placebo (n =156) (7.7 percent vs 16.8 percent; HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.21 - 0.83) and improved 3 year DFS (89.1% vs 78.7%; HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.29 - 0.88), while 5 year OS was not significantly different (93.0% vs 89.7% ; HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.30 - 1.51). Severe AEs occurred in 16.8% vs 11.6% with events including GI bleeding and subarachnoid hemorrhage, and one out of the 4 observed deaths was deemed possibly related to aspirin.

source.title: Low-Dose Aspirin for PI3K-Altered Localized Colorectal Cancer.

description: This part of the open-label multipart phase 3 trial, CheckMate 277 (Trial ID: 29658845), examined the performance of nivolumab plus ipilimumab compared to chemotherapy among non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients with a high tumour mutational burden (TMB) (>= 10 mutations/ megabase). Stage IV/ recurrent NSCLC patients that were chemotherapy treatment naïve were recruited. Patients with tumour programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression of at least 1% were randomly assigned to receive nivolumab plus ipilimumab, nivolumab monotherapy, or chemotherapy; while those with tumour PD-L1 expression of < 1% were randomly assigned to be treated with nivolumab plus ipilimumab, nivolumab plus chemotherapy, or chemotherapy. Tissue TMB was determined by the FoundationOne CDx assay. Patients with high TMB achieved significantly longer progression-free survival (PFS) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab (n = 139) (1-year PFS of 42%, median PFS of 7.2 months with 95% confidence interval [CI], 5.5 to 13.2), compared to chemotherapy alone (n = 160) (1-year PFS of 13.2%, median PFS of 5.5 months with 95% CI, 4.4 to 5.8) (hazard ratio [HR] 0.58; 97.5% CI, 0.41 to 0.81; P<0.001). 45.3% of patients achieved objective response with nivolumab plus ipilimumab, compared to 26.9% with chemotherapy. The benefit of nivolumab plus ipilimumab over chemotherapy was consistent across histologic subtypes and despite whether the tumour PD-L1 expression was at least 1% or lower than 1%. On the contrary, among the patients with low TMB, the clinical benefit was not significantly different between patients treated with nivolumab plus ipilimumab (n= 191) (median PFS of 3.2 months with 95% CI, 2.7 to 4.3) and those treated with chemotherapy (n=189) (median PFS of 5.5 months with 95% CI, 4.3 to 5.6) (HR 1.07; 95% CI, 0.84 to 1.35). In conclusion, this study demonstrated significant clinical benefit of first-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab over chemotherapy among NSCLC patients with a high TMB, irrespective of the expression level of tumour PD-L1.

source.title: Nivolumab plus Ipilimumab in Lung Cancer with a High Tumor Mutational Burden.

description:
In this 2025 retrospective study, 14 spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma (SCRMS) cases previously identified as possessing ZFP64::NCOA2 or ZFP64::NCOA3 fusions were pulled from clinical archives to assess clinicopathologic, immunohistochemical, and molecular genetic features. Key observations include a strong male prevalence, middle-age occurrence (median 41 years; range 22-81 years), wide anatomic distribution, and NCOA3 fusions are more common than NCOA2 fusions. Arising primarily from soft tissue, these tumors displayed both fascicular and spindle cell morphologies within a hyalinized collagenous background and various degrees of skeletal muscle marker expression, although occasional focal or diffuse round cell morphologies were also observed. 

All cases were analyzed by targeted RNA sequencing platforms from various laboratories, with specific fusions noted between ZFP64 exon 5::NCOA2 exon 14 fusion in 6 cases (43%) and ZFP64 exon 5::NCOA3 exon 14/15 fusion in 8 cases (57%). Ten of these cases were also characterized by DNA methylation profiling, revealing ZFP64 SCRMS as an epigenetic sarcoma subtype distinct from other RMS. SCRMS with ZFP64::NCOA2/3 fusions are associated with frequent distant metastases, local recurrences, and death, and therefore these fusions may provide benefit as prognostic markers.

source.title: Clinicopathologic and Molecular Genetic Features of Spindle Cell Rhabdomyosarcoma Harboring ZFP64::NCOA2/3 Fusions: A Series of 14 Cases.

description: The use of circulating tumor DNA in blood for TMB assessment was tested. The cancer gene panel NCC-GP150, which covers the whole exon regions of 150 genes, was created and tested for correlation against established methods for TMB assessment. Testing compared whole exome sequencing (WES) results from tissue samples of 48 Chinese advanced NSCLC patients with NCC-GP150 from matched blood samples from those patients. A Spearman correlation of 0.62 (P<0.001) was reported between these results, when the cutoff between high and low blood TMB (H-bTMB) was greater or equal to 6. In a test with 33 different cancer types, NCC-GP150 correlated strongly with established WES results in 25/33 of the tumor types. 50 advanced NSCLC patients were treated with PD-1 or PDL-1 inhibition. When the H-bTMB cutoff was set to 6, then a minimum hazard ratio favoring H-bTMB patients was seen of HR=0.39 (0.18-0.84) P=.02. For the subset of patients with anti-PD1/PD-L1 therapy as first- or second-Line treatment, results were stronger with HR=0.08 (0.02-0.36) P=.001 at a cutoff of H-bTMB of 6. In this subgroup overall response rate was significantly different (P=0.003), 61.1% in H-b-TMB and 6.7% in L-bTMB. Additionally, in responders bTMB was significantly higher (median 10) than in non responders (median 5, P=0.008). The authors conclude that  ctDNA-based bTMB measured using the NCC-GP150 panel is a potential biomarker for anti–PD-1 and anti–PD-L1 treatment in NSCLC.

source.title: Assessment of Blood Tumor Mutational Burden as a Potential Biomarker for Immunotherapy in Patients With Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer With Use of a Next-Generation Sequencing Cancer Gene Panel.

description: In this 2015 study, formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue samples were retrieved from the diagnostic pathology archives of the Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital (RNOH) and the Basel Bone Tumour Reference Centre (BBTRC). All cases were reviewed by specialist bone tumor pathologists at both institutions and classified according to the current World Health Organization (WHO) criteria. To investigate the oncogenic driver of Giant Cell Tumor of Bone (GCT), whole-genome sequencing was performed on 5 cases and whole-exome sequencing on 1 case. In addition, targeted hotspot sequencing using a 14-gene panel, including the paralogous genes H3F3A and H3F3B, was conducted to assess the specificity of the p.G34W alteration in GCT. This analysis included 91 GCT cases and 321 other osteoclast-rich bone lesions, such as aneurysmal bone cyst, chondroblastoma, non-ossifying fibroma, giant cell granuloma, and osteoclast-rich malignant bone tumors. The results showed that no driver mutations other than H3F3A p.G34W were identified in the sequenced genomes and exome. Targeted sequencing detected the H3F3A p.G34W mutation in 83 GCT cases, while H3F3A p.G34R and p.G34M mutations were each identified in one tumor. No mutations were detected in H3F3B. Both GCTs that had metastasized to the lung harbored the H3F3A p.G34W mutation. In conclusion, the presence of H3F3A p.G34 alterations in 96% (85/89) of GCTs and their absence in other bone tumors demonstrate that these mutations are highly sensitive and specific molecular markers for GCT.

source.title: Diagnostic value of H3F3A mutations in giant cell tumour of bone compared to osteoclast-rich mimics.

description: In this 2015 study, formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor samples originally diagnosed between 1996 and 2014 as giant cell tumor of bone (GCTB), chondroblastoma, chondromyxoid fibroma, aneurysmal bone cyst, or telangiectatic osteosarcoma were retrieved from the archives of the Department of Pathology at Leiden University Medical Centre (Leiden, The Netherlands). 75 GCTB samples were analyzed, including 15 recurrences from 12 patients. H3F3A hotspot mutations were identified using Sanger sequencing. Immunohistochemical analyses of H3K36 trimethylation and ATRX expression, previously proposed as surrogate markers in pediatric brain tumors, was performed to assess their correlation with H3F3A mutation status. The majority of GCTBs (n = 41) harbored H3F3A G34W or G34V mutations (39 G34W and 2 G34V). Additionally, one case exhibited a G34 stop codon mutation, and another showed a TCT insertion at position 35. H3K36 trimethylation was detected in 59 of 60 GCTB cases, including all 41 tumors with H3F3A G34W/V mutations, compared with GCTBs and other giant cell–containing tumors without these mutations. In contrast, loss of ATRX protein expression did not correlate with H3F3A mutation status. As it is unknown whether the non-G34W/V variants have the same effect as G34W/V, only G34W/V variants were categorized as mutation positive within immunohistochemistry correlation analysis. In conclusion, the results of this study showed that H3F3A mutation analysis using conventional Sanger sequencing on DNA extracted from decalcified FFPE tissue is a highly specific, although slightly less sensitive, diagnostic tool to distinguish GCTB from other giant cell–containing tumors of bone. Although immunohistochemistry for H3K36me3 and ATRX cannot be used as surrogate diagnostic markers, the findings suggest that H3F3A mutations are associated with increased trimethylation of H3K36 in GCTB. Future studies should reveal how methylation at this specific residue orchestrates tumorigenesis in GCTB.

source.title: Mutation Analysis of H3F3A and H3F3B as a Diagnostic Tool for Giant Cell Tumor of Bone and Chondroblastoma.

description:
In the breast carcinoma cohort of the phase II TAPUR trial (NCT02693535), patients with BRCA1/2 alterations treated with olaparib (26 evaluable) had 1 CR (BRCA2 loss), 11 PR (BRCA1 n=5, BRCA2 n=4, BRCA1/2 n=2), 6 SD16+ (BRCA1 n=1, BRCA2 n=4, BRCA1/2 n=1) yielding ORR 46% (95% CI, 27-67) and DCR 69% (90% CI 55-100; p < 0.001 vs null 15%). Median PFS was 26 weeks (95% CI 15–33) and median OS 55 weeks (95% CI 33–100) in this cohort.
Across all TAPUR cohorts combined (NCT02693535; n = 116 evaluable; BC n = 26, BTC n = 18, LC n = 25, UC n = 15, HP n = 32), patients with advanced solid tumors harboring BRCA1/2 alterations treated with olaparib achieved 13 CR, 15 PR, 20 SD≥16 weeks, and 68 PD, corresponding to an ORR of 24% (95% CI 17–33). The median duration of response was 31 weeks (range 7–284). Among patients with recent platinum exposure (n = 81), 43% achieved DC, including 15 OR (19%; 95% CI 11–29) and 20 SD16+ (25%; 95% CI 16–36).

source.title: Olaparib in Patients With Solid Tumors With BRCA1/2 Alterations: Results From The Targeted Agent and Profiling Utilization Registry (TAPUR) Study.

description:
In the biliary tract carcinoma cohort of the phase II TAPUR trial (NCT02693535), patients with BRCA1/2 alterations treated with olaparib (18 evaluable) had 2 PR (BRCA1 loss n = 1, BRCA2 mutation n = 1), 7 SD16+ (bile duct n=5, gallbladder n =2; BRCA1 n = 1, BRCA2 n = 4, BRCA1/2 n = 2) yielding an ORR of 11% (95% CI 1–35) and a DCR of 50% (90% CI 32–100; p = 0.0008 vs null 15%). The two PRs had DORs of 81 and 279 weeks, SD16+ had a median duration of 26 weeks (range 20–40), and median PFS and OS were 18 weeks (95% CI 8–26) and 47 weeks (95% CI 24–78), respectively.


Across all TAPUR cohorts combined (NCT02693535; n = 116 evaluable; BC n = 26, BTC n = 18, LC n = 25, UC n = 15, HP n = 32), patients with advanced solid tumors harboring BRCA1/2 alterations treated with olaparib achieved 13 CR, 15 PR, 20 SD≥16 weeks, and 68 PD, corresponding to an ORR of 24% (95% CI 17–33). The median duration of response was 31 weeks (range 7–284). Among patients with recent platinum exposure (n = 81), 43% achieved DC, including 15 OR (19%; 95% CI 11–29) and 20 SD16+ (25%; 95% CI 16–36).

source.title: Olaparib in Patients With Solid Tumors With BRCA1/2 Alterations: Results From The Targeted Agent and Profiling Utilization Registry (TAPUR) Study.

description: In this 2019 study, targeted RNA sequencing using the Archer FusionPlex technology was validated and implemented to detect oncogenic fusion transcripts in 62 genes recurrently rearranged in solid tumors, including sarcomas, without prior knowledge of fusion partners. A total of 192 formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) bone and soft tissue tumor samples from January 2016 to January 2018 were submitted to Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center for analysis. In-frame gene fusions were identified in 79 of 184 cases (43%), including 6 cases (3%) with novel fusion partners. In two cases of pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma present in this study cohort the testing revealed FOSB fusions with a novel partner gene ACTB. In both ACTB::FOSB fusion positive  pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma cases the ACTB exon 3 was joined with the FOSB exon 2. The FOSB breakpoint in the ACTB::FOSB fusion matched previously reported breakpoints. This study further confirms specific association between FOSB fusions and  pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma.

source.title: Diagnosis of known sarcoma fusions and novel fusion partners by targeted RNA sequencing with identification of a recurrent ACTB-FOSB fusion in pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma.

description:
This is part of a multi-centred, randomised, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial, CHOICE-01, that examined therapeutic response to first-line chemotherapy plus PD-1 inhibitor in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients to explore ctDNA-based stratification strategies.

405 treatment-naïve patients with either locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC that do not carry EGFR or ALK driver mutations were randomly assigned to receive toripalimab (n=309) or placebo (n = 156) in combination with chemotherapy. 371 of the 405 patients with pre-treatment ctDNA present (maximal somatic allele frequency of >=0.5%). Blood-based TMB (bTMB) measured by the 520-gene OncoCompass Plus panel (Burning Rock Biotech) was calculated as the number of small single-nucleotide variations (SNVs) and indels detected at an allele frequency of >=0.2% per Mb of coding regions of target genes (1.003 Mb for the panel used). 

Using 13 mutations/ Mb (top 20%) as the cut off, patients with high bTMB achieved greater progression free survival from chemotherapy plus PD-1 inhibitor compare dot the bTMB-low group (interaction p = 0.027). However, no difference in overall survival benefits from the addition of PD-1 inhibitor was observed between the two groups.

source.title: Circulating tumor DNA-based stratification strategy for chemotherapy plus PD-1 inhibitor in advanced non-small-cell lung cancer.

description: In this 2023 study, the authors evaluated the diagnostic utility of NR4A3 immunohistochemistry in acinic cell carcinoma (AciCC) of the salivary gland. The cohort included 128 AciCCs, comprising 85 classic low-grade, 36 with high-grade transformation (HGT), and 7 high-grade tumors. NR4A3 rearrangements were assessed using a custom dual-color break-apart FISH probe. NR4A3 immunoreactivity was observed in 105 of 128 cases (82%), with similar positivity rates across low-grade, HGT, and high-grade AciCCs (82%, 81%, and 86%, respectively). FISH analysis was performed in 57 cases, confirming NR4A3 rearrangements in 23 of 28 (82%) low-grade cases, 11 of 14 (79%) HGT cases, and 2 of 2 (100%) high-grade cases, resulting in an overall confirmation rate of 36 of 44 (82%) in analyzable immunopositive tumors. Eight immunopositive cases (18%) were FISH-negative, while among 10 immunonegative cases, 2 of 8 analyzable tumors (25%) demonstrated NR4A3 rearrangement. Five cases were not evaluable by FISH. The authors conclude that NR4A3 rearrangements are strongly associated with AciCC and that NR4A3 immunohistochemistry is a robust and reliable tool for the differential diagnosis of this tumor.

source.title: A minority of cases of acinic cell carcinoma of the salivary glands are driven by an NR4A2 rearrangement: the diagnostic utility of the assessment of NR4A2 and NR4A3 alterations in salivary gland tumors.

description: In this 2019 study, the authors aimed to evaluate the usefulness of NR4A3 immunostaining and compare it with NR4A3 Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) for the differential diagnosis of acinic cell carcinoma (AciCC). The study included 64 AciCC cases (53 low-grade tumors and 11 with high-grade transformation), 29 mammary analogue secretory carcinoma (MASC), and 70 other salivary gland carcinomas, evaluated by NR4A3 immunostaining. NR4A3 immunostaining was considered positive when moderate to strong nuclear staining was observed, while cytoplasmic staining was regarded as nonspecific. Moderate to strong nuclear NR4A3 expression was detected in 63 of 64 AciCCs (98%), including all high-grade transformed cases; only one case was negative. In contrast, none of the MASCs or other salivary gland carcinomas showed nuclear NR4A3 staining. These findings confirmed specific association of the NR4A3 rearrangement and upregulation with AciCC. FISH analysis was successfully performed in 58 AciCCs, of which 49 cases (84%) showed abnormal NR4A3 signals consistent with gene translocation (44 with split signals and 5 with single red signals). Nine cases (16%) showed normal FISH results. Samples were classified as positive when more than 20% of 50 counted nuclei displayed abnormal signals. The authors concluded that NR4A3 rearrangement is highly associated with AciCC and the immunostaining is sensitive and specific marker for AciCC, including high-grade cases. The studies shows utility of confirming NR4A3 rearrangement by immunostaining and FISH in distinguishing AciCC from MASC.

source.title: Nuclear NR4A3 Immunostaining Is a Specific and Sensitive Novel Marker for Acinic Cell Carcinoma of the Salivary Glands.

description: This was a retrospective analysis of genetic markers in 503 metastatic colorectal cancer patients who participated in the CORRECT phase III trial of regorafenib. Authors found a clinical benefit of regorafenib across PIK3CA mutated and wildtype subgroups (progression free survival with regorafenib vs placebo: mutant HR: 0.54, wildtype HR: 0.50, P=0.85). Authors do not provide direct comparison between patients with wildtype and PIK3CA E542K patients. Note that it's unclear how many PIK3CA wildtype patients harbor KRAS mutations, though authors' suggest that regorafenib induces clinical benefit regardless of KRAS or PIK3CA mutation status.

This was a Phase I and II study (NCT01072175) of dabrafenib and trametinib combination therapy vs. dabrafenib monotherapy in patients with metastatic melanoma.  

Cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma was seen in 7% of patients receiving combination therapy in contrast to 19% in those receiving monotherapy (P = 0.09).

Of 162 patients with V600E or V600K mutation, 108 were given combination therapy and 54 monotherapy.

After 1 year, 41% of patients in the combination group were alive and progression free whereas this was 9% in the monotherapy group (P<0.001).


Median progression-free survival was 9.4 months with combination and 5.8 months with monotherapy. Hazard ratio for progression or death was 0.39 (95% CI, 0.25 to 0.62; P<0.001).

description:
In this publication, the role of NPM1 mutations in defining a distinct subset of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) was investigated. Among 1,485 adult AML patients enrolled in the multicenter AML96 protocol, fragment analysis and Sanger sequencing identified NPM1 insertion mutations in 27.5% of cases, most commonly within the terminal coding exon (historically referred to as exon 12). These mutations resulted in cytoplasmic mislocalization of the NPM1 protein, a feature confirmed by confocal microscopy.
The study demonstrated that NPM1 mutations occur most frequently in AML patients with a normal karyotype and are strongly associated with characteristic clinicopathologic features, including higher leukocyte and blast counts. NPM1 mutations were found in conjunction with FLT3-ITDs (internal tandem duplications) in 40.2% (164/408) of patients. Analysis of the mutant/wild type ratio for patients harboring both NPM1 mutations and FLT3-ITDs indicated that NPM1 mutations were present in a higher percent of blasts, suggesting they are a primary event in AML patients, preceding the acquisition of FLT3-ITD mutations.
From a clinical perspective, the presence of an NPM1 mutation was shown to confer a distinct biological entity with prognostic implications. Patients with NPM1-mutated AML, in the absence of FLT3-ITDs, had significantly improved overall survival, disease-free survival, and lower relapse incidence compared with other AML subgroups. Multivariate analysis confirmed that NPM1 mutations alone represent an independent favorable prognostic factor.
This study identified AML with mutated NPM1 as a common, biologically distinct entity, marked by elevated bone marrow blasts, increased white blood cell and platelet counts, a higher incidence in females, association with a normal karyotype, frequent co-occurrence of FLT3 mutations, and favorable outcomes in cases lacking FLT3 mutations.

description: This was a retrospective study of 691 cetuximab treated patients with metastatic, chemotherapy refractory colorectal cancer. Of those, 30 patients harbored BRAF V600E, were KRAS, NRAS and PIK3CA wt, and had individual response data. One patient (who harbored BRAF V600E in low copy number) responded, 11 had stable disease, and 18 progressed. Treatments included cetuximab + irinotecan (n=20), cetuximab monotherapy (n=5), cetuximab + FOLFIRI (n=4), and cetuximab + oxaliplatin + 5FU (n=1). Median PFS was 8 weeks (2-32 weeks), median OS was 25 weeks (4-237 weeks), and median number of previous chemotherapy lines was 2 (0-4). Median age was 61 years old (42-78) and there were 16 males and 14 females. Authors concluded that BRAF mutation (23/24 of mutants were BRAF V600E) was strongly associated with poor response to cetuximab and suggested that mutation status of BRAF is more informative than those of NRAS and PIK3CA exon 20 for predicting cetuximab response (second only to KRAS).

Germline presence of the T allele increased the risk of glioblastoma development (adjusted odds ratio, 1.96; P = .013). source.title: Nuclear DICKKOPF-1 as a biomarker of chemoresistance and poor clinical outcome in colorectal cancer.

description: 72 patients with malignant pleural mesothelioma were analyzed, MDM2 immunoexpression was assessed in 65 patients. MDM2 mRNA and protein expression correlated with poor OS and PFS for patients treated with standard of care therapy (cisplatin and pemetrexed).

description: mRNA expression of thymidylate synthase (TYMS) in 62 NSCLC patients correlated with response rate to pemetrexed mono- or combination therapy. Response rate with low TYMS expression was 0.29 compared with 0.03 in patients with overexpression (P = 0.025). Patients with low expression exhibited a benefit in time to progression (average TTP = 56 vs. 23 months, P = 0.001) and in overall survival (average OS = 60 vs. 25 months, P = 0.002).

description: In this meta-analysis (14 studies, 1021 patients), EGFR gene copy number (GCN) was predictive of improved progression free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) with cetuximab or panitumumab regardless of KRAS status. description: This prospective study enrolled 31 Enzalutamide-treated (group 1) and 31 Abiraterone-treated (group 2) patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancers (CRPC). description: 498 patients were retrospectively analyzed for topoisomerase 1 expression (IHC). description: While EGFR mutation is a strong predictive factor for EGFR inhibition, some patients with EGFR wild-type also respond.  The authors investigated whether phosphorylated EGFR could be a potential predictive biomarker in patients with wild-type EGFR. Phosphorylation of Y1068 (assessed by IHC) was associated with improved progression free survival (PFS) in 205 patients with stage IIb and IV NSCLC treated with EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (gefitinib or erlotinib) compared to phospho-Y1068 negative patients (median PFS 7.0 months vs. 1.2 months, P < 0.001). In this group, 92 (44.9%) were EGFR mutant. In a subgroup of patients with wild-type EGFR, phospho-Y1068 expression positive patients had a significantly prolonged PFS (4.2 months vs.1.2 months P < 0.001) compared with those without phospho-Y1068 expression.

source.title: Phosphorylated EGFR expression may predict outcome of EGFR-TKIs therapy for the advanced NSCLC patients with wild-type EGFR.

description: Absent/low expression of BRCA1 (IHC) was associated with improved response to chemotherapy in 292 patients with sporadic ovarian cancer compared to patients with high expression (odds ratio 2.47: 95%CI 1.10-5.55, p=0.029).

source.title: BRCA1 is both a prognostic and predictive biomarker of response to chemotherapy in sporadic epithelial ovarian cancer.

description: A phase II study involving adult female patients, >=18 years, with stage IIIB or IV HER2-positive (by IHC and/or in situ fluorescence) metastatic breast cancer. All patients were previously treated with trastuzumab and a median of three chemotherapy lines. 41 patients received 50 mg afatinib once-daily until disease progression and the primary endpoint was objective response rate. 4 patients (10% of 41 treated; 11% of evaluable patients) had partial response and 15 patients (37% of 41) had stable disease as best response. Thus a total of 19 (46% of 41) achieved clinical benefit. Median progression-free survival was 15.1 weeks.

description: An EGFR resistance mutation, C797S, was discovered by deep sequencing of cell-free plasma DNA (cfDNA) from patients with advanced lung cancer whose tumors had developed resistance to osimertinib. Expression of this mutant EGFR construct in a cell line rendered it resistant to osimertinib. ddPCR on serial cfDNA specimens collected from 15 osimertinib-treated subjects (all positive for T790M before treatment) revealed 6 cases with acquired C797S mutation.

source.title: Acquired EGFR C797S mutation mediates resistance to AZD9291 in non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR T790M.

description: This study summarized 9 EGFR-mutant patients from two clinical trials involving rociletinib (NCT01526928) and subsequent osimertinib (NCT01802632). 8 were T790M-positive prior to treatment with osimertinib. 6 transitioned directly from rociletinib to osimertinib. 3 patients achieved PR and 4 achieved SD. The median PFS was 208 days (95% CI, 41-208 days). Among 6 patients who transitioned directly from rociletinib to osimertinib all derived clinical benefit from osimertinib with either prolonged SD or PR.

description: In a Phase II clinical trial, patients with Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM), positive for EGFR VIII deletion mutation (N=65), were treated with the Rindopepimut cancer vaccine,  and standard adjuvant temozolomide chemotherapy.  Median progression free survival (PFS) was 9.2 months, and median overall survival (OS) was 21.8 months.  A pivotal, randomized Phase III trial is currently underway.

description: Serum and tissue levels of HER2 (ERBB2) were analyzed in 1,902 breast cancer patients treated with lapatinib or control. description: 172 patients treated with neoadjuvant concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) were retrospectively analyzed for expression of thrombospondin 2 (THBS2) using IHC (discovery set with 46 rectal cancer patients, GSE35452). description: Melanoma patients treated with Anti-PD1 or anti-PD-L1(nivolumab, pembrolizumab, MPDL3280A) therapy were analyzed for expression of HLA-DRA (the primary antigen-presenting molecule of the MHC-II pathway). In a discovery cohort, 30 patients underwent IHC for HLA-DRA. 11/14 (79%) patients with positive HLA-DR staining, had complete (n=3) or partial (n=8) response. 6/16 (38%) HLA-DR non-expressing melanomas responded to therapy (overall response rate 79 versus 38%, Fisher’s exact test P=0.033). This finding was confirmed in a second independent data set of 23 melanoma patients with 6/8 (75%) of HLA-DR(+) tumours in comparison to 4/15 (27%) HLA-DR(−) responding (Fisher’s exact test P=0.025). Preclinical models confirmed the result.
